text: And things went downhill fast. The Black Death, or bubonic plague, tore through towns and cities
like a biological wildfire. Caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis, it traveled on
rats, fleas, and humans who had absolutely no concept of personal hygiene. Once it hit,
survival became a lottery. You could catch it from a handshake, a shared cup,
or just by breathing the same medieval air as an infected guy. Symptoms included giant
swollen lymph nodes, fever, vomiting blood, and, spoiler alert, death, usually within days.
